summary: search locates the first regular-expression match and returns its zero-based starting index.
documentation: search locates the first regular-expression match and returns its zero-based starting index. No match returns -1. It reports a position rather than the full matching text, and it does not use a regex lastIndex as a starting offset.
caution: A pattern can match inside a larger token unless boundaries are specified. The marker grammar here deliberately permits substring matches.
scenarios: Jump to the first structured error marker in a pasted log.
Highlight the first ticket reference in a support note.
Find the first expected code pattern during an import preview.
title: Locate the first ticket marker
problem: Return the starting index of the first substring matching uppercase T- followed by three ASCII digits. T-1234 contains a valid match T-123. Return -1 when no match exists.
hint: Search for /T-[0-9]{3}/ without a global flag.
goal: Use String.search() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
